thread:
anna: Heads up — running into a weird socket timeout only on the Android emulator when our Kotlin SDK (Retrofit + OkHttp) talks to the staging API. Works fine on device and desktop.
raj: Which emulator image? network config? :thinking_face:
anna: Pixel 2 API 30 emulator. Host: https://staging-api.redwood.example (we're using a cert from our internal CA). Happens during TLS handshake, then OkHttp throws SocketTimeoutException on connect.
marc: Do you see any TLS version mismatch logs? Android default TLS config can be surprising on older APIs.
anna: No obvious stacktrace aside from connect -> SocketTimeoutException. I've enabled OkHttp logging interceptor and here's the tail:
```
D/OkHttp: --> GET https://staging-api.redwood.example/v1/health
D/OkHttp: connectionSpec = ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT? false
W/OkHttp: TLS handshake timed out after 10000ms
E/OkHttp: java.net.SocketTimeoutException: failed to connect to staging-api.redwood.example/10.0.2.2 (port 443) from /10.0.2.15 (port 56734) after 10000ms
```
raj: 10.0.2.2 is the emulator host mapping; are you doing any port-forwarding? Could be emulator -> host proxy + CA chain not trusted.
anna: Port forwarding is set. Host has our internal reverse proxy that negotiates TLSv1.3. Emulator API 30 supports TLS 1.3 but the Chain uses some ECDSA curves. Works on real device.
marc: OkHttp's ConnectionSpec defaults changed across versions. If the client negotiates TLSv1.3 but the JDK/conscrypt on the emulator doesn't like the cipher, handshake could hang. Try forcing ConnectionSpec.COMPATIBLE_TLS or a TLS 1.2-only spec as a repro.
emily: Also try `enableTlsExtensions(true)` and explicitly set `ConnectionSpec.MODERN_TLS`? On Android you often need conscrypt fallback.
anna: Tried setting:
```
val client = OkHttpClient.Builder()
  .connectionSpecs(listOf(ConnectionSpec.MODERN_TLS, ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT))
  .connectTimeout(10, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .readTimeout(30, TimeUnit.SECONDS)
  .build()
```
Still hangs on handshake.
raj: Two more checks: 1) ensure emulator trusts the CA (Network Security Config or install CA on emulator). 2) try disabling TLS 1.3 at the proxy if possible to see if TLS 1.2 works.
anna: I installed the CA cert into the emulator system store; no change. Disabling TLS 1.3 on proxy made it work reliably.
marc: That strongly suggests a TLS 1.3 compatibility issue in the emulator's TLS stack or the cipher suites negotiation. OkHttp can fallback but only if it detects the failure — sometimes the handshake hangs instead of failing fast.
emily: One trick we've used: wrap the connect in a separate OkHttp call that pre-connects to `/health` with a short timeout and retries with a modified ConnectionSpec on failure.
raj: Example pattern:
```
fun buildClient(forceTls12: Boolean = false): OkHttpClient {
  val specs = if (forceTls12) {
    listOf(ConnectionSpec.RESTRICTED_TLS, ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT)
  } else {
    listOf(ConnectionSpec.MODERN_TLS, ConnectionSpec.COMPATIBLE_TLS, ConnectionSpec.CLEARTEXT)
  }
  return OkHttpClient.Builder()
    .connectionSpecs(specs)
    .build()
}

// preflight
try { client.newCall(Request.Builder().url(url).get().build()).execute() } catch (e: SocketTimeoutException) { // try fallback }
```
anna: That workaround is fine for testing but not great for onboarding docs. Any ideas to make SDK default robust for emulator/dev setups?
marc: We could add auto-detect: if running on emulator (check ro.build.characteristics or android.os.Build.FINGERPRINT contains 'generic'), prefer ConnectionSpec.COMPATIBLE_TLS or TLS1.2-first policy. Document this in the Android SDK quickstart.
emily: Also update the sample app to include a Network Security Config snippet and instructions to install the CA for system trust. Show how to toggle a `SDK_EMULATOR_FALLBACK=true` env var in gradle for sample builds.
anna: Will open a tiny PR: 1) detect emulator and prefer compatible TLS, 2) add a short note in docs about TLS 1.3 emulator issues + dev workaround. Also add a reproducible snippet for maintainers.
raj: Can you paste the minimal repro steps so QA can try? I'll spin an emulator image later.
anna: Repro steps in short:
- Android Studio emulator Pixel 2 API 30
- Host reverse proxy at 10.0.2.2:443 with TLS 1.3 and ECDSA chain
- App uses Retrofit 2.9 + OkHttp 4.9.3 default client
- call to /v1/health hangs on TLS handshake -> SocketTimeoutException after connectTimeout
- disabling TLS 1.3 at proxy or forcing ConnectionSpec.RESTRICTED_TLS on client fixes it

raj: Good, please file the PR and link the test matrix (emulator images + okHttp versions) so we can track.
